method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **The aim of initial assessment is to identify and treat serious causes.**
claims.source_text: There are many causes of an acutely swollen joint. The aim of initial assessment is to identify and treat serious ones
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Acute inability to walk or weight bear is a red flag.**
claims.source_text: Acute inability to walk or weight bear is a red flag
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspect septic arthritis — an orthopaedic emergency — in any child with localised severe joint pain and swelling, especially with fever.**
claims.source_text: Septic arthritis is an orthopaedic emergency and should be suspected in any child presenting with localised severe joint pain and swelling, especially with fever
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children discharged with an unclear diagnosis need early follow-up.**
claims.source_text: Children discharged with an unclear diagnosis require early follow up
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute = onset under 2 weeks.** Note site and character (migratory, early morning).
claims.source_text: Joint swelling: site, onset (<2 weeks is acute), character (migratory/early morning)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about** constant severe or night pain; systemic features (weight loss, fatigue, night sweats, rash, unexplained bruising, visual impairment, diarrhoea); **family history of haemophilia** or autoimmune/inflammatory disease.
claims.source_text: Constant severe pain or night pain … Systemic features: Weight loss/fatigue/night sweats, rash, unexplained bruising, visual impairment, diarrhoea … Family history: haemophilia, autoimmune or inflammatory conditions
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **ARF risk groups:** Indigenous Australians, Māori and Pacific Islanders; personal or family history of ARF or rheumatic heart disease.
claims.source_text: Groups at risk for acute rheumatic fever (ARF): Indigenous Australians, Maori and Pacific Islanders; personal or family history of ARF or rheumatic heart disease
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look, feel, move — start with the non-painful side.** Also check for pallor, lymphadenopathy, petechiae or purpura, hepatosplenomegaly and abdominal mass.
claims.source_text: Joint and limb assessment using the “Look, feel, move”, start with non-painful side … Haematological: Pallor, lymphadenopathy, petechiae/ecchymosis/purpura Abdominal: Hepatosplenomegaly, abdominal mass
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Septic arthritis / osteomyelitis:** severe localised joint or limb pain, systemic features, acute fever; commonly lower-limb joints.
claims.source_text: Infection Septic arthritis/ Osteomyelitis Severe localised joint and/or limb pain Systemic features, fever (acute onset) Commonly lower limb joints
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Child abuse:** unexplained injury or bruising, particularly in a non-ambulatory child.
claims.source_text: Child abuse Unexplained injury, bruising Particularly if non ambulatory child
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reactive arthritis:** after pharyngitis, gastroenteritis or urethritis (Chlamydia), onset 7–14 days later; oligo- or monoarticular, usually lower limbs.
claims.source_text: Reactive Reactive arthritis Recent illness: pharyngitis, gastroenteritis, urethritis (Chlamydia) Onset 7 to 14 days later Oligo/monoarticular arthritis, normally lower limbs
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haemophilia:** personal or family history, unexplained bruising or bleeding; most commonly the knee.
claims.source_text: Haematological Haemophilia Personal/Family history Unexplained bruising/bleeding Most commonly knee
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **JIA / mixed connective tissue disease:** fever, rash, oligo- or polyarthritis, enthesitis, psoriasis; the child can normally weight bear.
claims.source_text: Rheumatological Juvenile idiopathic arthritis/mixed connective tissue disease Fever, rash Oligo/polyarticular arthritis Enthesitis Psoriasis Haematuria Hepatosplenomegaly Normally can weight bear
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kawasaki disease:** fever over 5 days with rash, conjunctivitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, swollen hands and feet.
claims.source_text: Other systemic inflammatory disorders Kawasaki disease Prolonged fever >5 days Rash, conjunctivitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, swelling of hands and feet
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Acute rheumatic fever:** at-risk population, fever, **migratory polyarthritis or arthralgia of large joints**, murmur (mitral or aortic regurgitation); skin signs are rare.
claims.source_text: Acute rhematic fever (ARF) At risk population Fever Migratory polyarthritis/arthralgia – usually large joints Heart murmur (mitral or aortic regurgitation) Skin changes (erythema marginatum/subcutaneous nodules) – seen rarely
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **HSP:** purpuric rash, usually lower limbs, with lower-limb joints affected.
claims.source_text: Vasculitis Henoch-Schönlein purpura Purpuric rash (normally affecting lower limbs) Usually lower limb joints affected
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Malignancy (leukaemia, bone or soft-tissue tumour):** fever, weight loss, lethargy, night sweats, **nocturnal pain**, pallor, bruising, hepatosplenomegaly or abdominal mass.
claims.source_text: Malignancy Leukaemia Bone/soft tissue malignancy/ Solid organ tumour Fever, weight loss, lethargy, fatigue, anorexia, night sweats, Nocturnal pain Pallor, bruising Hepatosplenomegaly/abdominal mass
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No investigations may be needed** if there are no red flags and there is a clear working diagnosis and/or a plan to review within 7 days.
claims.source_text: Consider no investigations if: No red flags A clear working diagnosis and/or a plan to review within 7 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat according to the working diagnosis**, with pain management (consider immobilisation) and child-directed limitation of activity.
claims.source_text: Definitive management is determined by the working diagnosis … Pain management: see acute pain management and consider immobilization Child-directed limitation of activity
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Septic arthritis: consult the orthopaedic team.** For infective causes, refer to the relevant sub-specialty team and follow local antibiotic guidelines.
claims.source_text: Septic arthritis is an orthopaedic emergency - consult local orthopaedic team … For infective causes, refer to the appropriate sub-specialist team and consult local antibiotic guidelines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected ARF:** discuss with a paediatrician experienced in ARF, an ID physician or a paediatric cardiologist; **echocardiogram even without a murmur**; **avoid NSAIDs during the diagnostic workup** — they may mask migratory joint symptoms.
claims.source_text: Acute rheumatic fever: All suspected cases should be discussed with a paediatrician experienced in ARF, ID physician or paediatric cardiologist An echocardiogram is required even if no clinical murmur to exclude subclinical carditis Avoid NSAIDS during diagnostic workup, as these may mask migratory joint symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the paediatric team** for suspected child abuse or an unclear diagnosis.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Suspected child abuse Diagnosis is unclear
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Refer:** suspected septic arthritis → orthopaedics; **suspected haemarthrosis in known or suspected haemophilia → haematology**; joint pain over 4 weeks, multiple joints, or vasculitis other than HSP → rheumatology.
claims.source_text: Refer for specialist assessment if: Suspected septic arthritis (orthopaedics) Suspected haemarthrosis in a known or suspected haemophiliac (haematology) Joint pain >4 weeks and/or multiple joints involved, or vasculitis other than HSP (rheumatology)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge** when the cause is identified and managed — or, **if the diagnosis is unclear**, only when pain is controlled **and** high-risk diagnoses are excluded **and** follow-up is arranged.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when The cause of the swollen joint has been identified and appropriately managed If the diagnosis is unclear: The child’s pain is adequately managed AND High risk diagnoses have been considered and excluded AND Appropriate follow up has been arranged
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'The acutely swollen joint' (Last updated October 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/The_acutely_swollen_joint/, retrieved 2026-09-23
